overview: The Medical & Wellness Tourism Policy is a scheme under the Ministry of Tourism aimed at promoting India as a destination for medical and wellness tourism. It seeks to leverage India's traditional healthcare systems and modern medical facilities to attract international patients. The policy focuses on infrastructure development, service quality enhancement, and global marketing of medical and wellness tourism offerings.
objectives: Promote India as a global destination for medical and wellness tourism
Enhance infrastructure and service quality in medical and wellness tourism sectors
Increase foreign tourist arrivals for medical and wellness purposes
Strengthen coordination between central and state governments for tourism development
Leverage traditional Indian systems like Ayurveda, Yoga, and Naturopathy
Improve global visibility of India's medical and wellness tourism offerings
eligibility: The Tourism Service Providers must be approved by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, or by the concerned State / Union Territory Tourism Department. The approved Tourism Service Providers showing minimum FEE of Rs. 1.00 crore – Rs. 2.00 crore in any one of the preceding two (2) years i.e. 2018-19 or 2019-20, the number of tours may be limited to maximum of two (02) in one financial year. The approved Tourism Service Providers showing minimum FEE of Rs. 2.00 crore and above in any one of the preceding two (2) years i.e. 2018-19 or 2019-20, the number of tours may be limited to maximum of three (03) in one financial year. Tourism Departments of State Governments / UT Administrations are also eligible to avail benefits under the Scheme. However, the above eligibility conditions are NOT applicable to them.
benefits: Financial support for Study Tours, participation in travel shows / exhibitions/ Road Shows (organized by the Ministry of Tourism) in the overseas markets would be extended as per following details, subject to an overall ceiling of Rs. 3.50 Lakh per case / tour: Economy class air fare for travel between India to another country and from there to a group of countries by air / rail at 90%; Cost of built up / furnished stall, electricity and water charges, participation fee, etc., at travel fair / exhibitions held overseas at 90%; Lodging expenses on overseas tour Max. 5 nights with an upper ceiling of room rate at Rs. 10,000/- per night. Financial support for participation in travel shows / exhibitions / in the overseas markets would be extended for Tourism Departments of State Governments / UT Administrations as per following details: Cost of built up / furnished stall, electricity and water charges, participation fee, etc., at travel fair / exhibitions held overseas with an overall ceiling of Rs. 3.50 Lakh. Financial support would be extended for Online Promotion of tourism destinations and products, tour packages in the overseas markets, including content creation / production of digital promotional brochures / leaflets etc. @ 50% of the total cost with an upper ceiling of Rs. 1.00 lakh/- once in a financial year, subject to actuals.

application_process: 1. The eligible TSP/SG/UT shall obtain Prior Approval of the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, before undertaking tour overseas. 2. The application as at Annexure -I for Prior Approval, shall be submitted to the Assistant Director General (Overseas Marketing), Government of India, Ministry of Tourism, on e-mail: mda-tourism@gov.in at least 21 days in advance prior to undertaking tour. 3. Prior Approval shall be granted subject to receipt of application complete in all respect. 4. After undertaking the tourism promotional activity/tour abroad for which Prior Approval had been accorded by the Ministry of Tourism, the Tourism Service Provider / State Govt./ UT Administration will submit the application for re -imbursement/claim, in the prescribed / applicable formats placed at Annexures – II, III & IV to the Assistant Director General (Overseas Marketing), Ministry of Tourism, Govt. of India, Transport Bhawan, 1, Parliament Street, New Delhi 110 001 on email mda-tourism@nic.in positively within a period of 45 days of completion of the activity. 5. Submission of claims in physical form will not be accepted. All documents submitted should be in pdf format only.
required_documents: Self-certified copy of proof of approval of the company by Ministry of Tourism or by the State Government/UT Administration

Declaration / Undertaking with official seal, date and on letter head of the company to the effect that the claimant is not under any investigation and/or has not been charged/prosecuted/debarred/ blacklisted by the Ministry of Tourism, Govt. of India/ Dept. of Tourism State Govt./UT Administration or any other Government agency.

Certificate of Foreign Exchange Earnings duly certified by Chartered Accountant as per details given at para 7 (ii) of the guidelines. The Certificate must also indicate the membership number of the Chartered Accountant.
Details of financial assistance availed during the last three years under the MDA Scheme, from the Government including Ministry of Commerce/FIEO & Ministry of Tourism.
Air ticket(s) for journeys performed along with Boarding Pass for each sector OR first page of the passport along with pages containing immigration stamps (entry/exit)
Tour Report in max. 250 words indicating the details of the activity participated / undertaken, outcome of the activity participated/undertaken (format at Annexure IV)
Original receipts/bank advice, etc., as proof of payments made for air tickets / booth / participation fee/ hotel accommodation, as the case may be, for which reimbursement is being claimed
deadlines: Financial support under the Scheme would be subject to availability of budget during the year under the MDA Scheme.
caveats: In case of more applications, priority would be given to those service providers who have not availed financial assistance in the past, under the MDA Scheme.
Incomplete applications are liable for rejection.

The claim for financial assistance must be submitted within 45 days from the date of return to India. Claim received after 45 days of return to India, or wherein the deficiencies in the claim as intimated are not fully completed within 45 days from the date of information/documents sought, will be rejected.
Financial support under the Scheme would be subject to availability of budget during the year under the MDA Scheme.
For reimbursement of air fare under the MDA Scheme, all tourism service provider shall travel only by Air India from India to stations abroad directly connected by Air India.

For travel from India to stations abroad, NOT directly connected by Air India, but are directly connected by other private airlines, travel by shorter route would be permissible on economy class only.

Tickets should be booked directly from Air India or from their online portal. In the case of travel by other private airlines for those sectors where Air India is not available, tickets should be booked directly from the online portal of the private airline or directly through the office of the private airline and not through an agency.
The TSP shall not be under investigation or charged/ prosecuted/debarred/black listed by Ministry of Tourism, Govt. of India or any other Government Agency.
The TSP should not have claimed/received any financial assistance for the Promotional Activity for which reimbursement is being claimed, from the Central / State Government or any Government Agency.
Details of financial assistance availed during the last three years including the current year, from the Ministry of Tourism or any Government agency, should be furnished.
